newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission proposes 2.4 pct rise for 1998 budget.
newsitem.headline: Commission proposes 2.4 pct rise for 1998 budget.

text.p: The European Commission opened the bidding for the EU's 1998 budget on Wednesday, proposing a 2.4 percent rise in committed expenditure totalling more than 91 billion European currency units ($103 billion).
Wednesday's proposal is only the first call in the yearly budget tussle between the Commission, the European Parliament and the Council of Ministers, which usually ends in December.
The 2.4 percent rise contrasts with last year's rise of four percent and the 8.1 percent of the year previously, European Budget Commissioner Erkki Liikanen told a news conference.
Farm spending remains way in front in the EU budgetary stakes, swallowing just under 41 billion ecus of the funds committed for the 1998 budget, albeit with a rise of not even half a percent on 1997.

Aid for the EU's poorer countries and regions, which is governed by binding commitments made in 1992, is due to increase its share of the cake in 1998 with a Commission proposal for a 6.3 percent rise to more than 33 billion ecus.

The Commission proposed nearly two percent more money for internal European Union policies such as research, transport networks, fisheries and the internal market, and a slightly smaller rise in spending on foreign policy.

Liikanen also announced a 4.4 billion ecu underpsend in the 1996 budget, which he said meant that countries' contributions to this year's budget would be reduced by that amount. The money was saved mostly in agriculture and regional aid, the two biggest budget lines.
He said the amount was less than the 9 billion ecus left unspent in 1995, when new regional aid programmes were slow to come on stream.
